messages.author: 665b3d97beb30882
messages.subject: Re: BioGeoBears google group and assistance
parts:
Hi Graeme,

You have a big analysis (11 areas, 6 max, equals:

numstates_from_numareas(numareas=11, maxareas=6, include_null_range=TRUE)

= 1486 states, i.e., exponentiating a 1486x1486 matrix for each branch each time the likelihood is calculated. )

This runs very slow on my machine at the moment as many of my processors are occupied. So it will be awhile before I could run your data thoroughly.



However, looking at your error output, it looks like not everything is up-to-date, and this is just an error resulting from an old function trying to read the parameter results and likelihoods out of the optimx results object.

Make sure:

1. You have optimx updated to the most recent version on CRAN, and all dependencies installed.

2. Make sure you source() ALL of the updated .R files at the beginning of the PhyloWiki example script every time you start a new R session / new BioGeoBEARS analysis. Just copy and paste those source() and cmpfun() commands into your personal script.

Let me know if this fixes it.

Cheers!
Nick



On Thu, Sep 4, 2014 at 4:14 AM, Graeme Oatley <graeme...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear Nick,

I have recently started using BioGeoBEARS and I would like to be added to the google group.

I have been successful in running the example files, however, my data always seems to return an error.
This is what I get at the end of the runs: 

Error in params_into_BioGeoBEARS_model_object(BioGeoBEARS_model_object,  : replacement has length zero
In addition: Warning message:
In (function (npt = min(n + 2L, 2L * n), rhobeg = NA, rhoend = NA,  :
  unused control arguments ignored

I searched the googlegroup for this error, and you suggested lengthening the branch lengths (some of our branch lengths are quite short), and then adjusting the min and max of the free parameters (although that was for the BayArea + j run, and I'm interested in doing DEC and DEC+j). 

I have done both, but still get the same error.

I have attached the R script I used most recently, two newick files (normal and lengthened branch lengths), and the geo file. I am running these analyses on a Windows 8 laptop.

Best, and thanks in advance
Graeme

Checking in from a meeting... So the path error indicates that your geography file is not actually being found. Double check your working directory and file ne and that the early part of the script actually reads the geog file...

The params_into error probably indicates you changed or left out something in the model setup, carefully run the example script line by line and check that everything is working, then do the same with your data.

There is a chance the optimx people changed something but I don't think so...
